#!/bin/bash

# Flux directives translated from SLURM
# The SLURM request for 18 tasks on one node for a single matlab command is
# interpreted as a request for 1 task with 18 CPUs.
#FLUX: -N 1
#FLUX: -n 1
#FLUX: -c 18
#FLUX: -t 01:00:00
#FLUX: -o "laporta_grid_study_nvib_bolsig_linear.out"

#
# --- Omitted SLURM options and explanations ---
#
# --mem=8G
#   Omitted. Flux does not have a direct batch script directive for memory.
#   Performance implication: Without a memory constraint, the job may be
#   scheduled on a node with insufficient memory, potentially causing it to
#   fail with an out-of-memory error or perform poorly due to heavy swapping.
#
# --job-name="glap_bol_lin"
#   Omitted. The job name in Flux is generally set during submission (e.g.,
#   'flux submit --job-name=... ...') or via the FLUX_JOB_NAME
#   environment variable, not through a script directive.
#

module load matlab/R2022a
module load intel

# There is a resource mismatch in the original script. It requests 18 tasks/cores
# but sets OMP_NUM_THREADS to 8. This means 10 of the allocated cores would be idle.
# This translation preserves the request for 18 cores, but the user should be aware
# of this inefficiency.
export omp_num_threads=8

cd /home/lynch/boltzmann_solvers/mtmhbe_solver/performance/laporta/grid_study/nvib_sweep_data/
matlab -nodisplay -nosplash -nodesktop -r "laporta_bolsig_linear;exit;"

issues: There is a significant resource mismatch in the script. It requests 18 CPU cores (`-c 18`) but then explicitly limits the number of OpenMP threads to 8 (`export omp_num_threads=8`). As the script's own comments correctly note, if the Matlab application's parallelism is controlled by this variable, 10 of the allocated cores (over 55% of the allocation) will be left completely idle, which is a highly inefficient use of resources.

As correctly noted in the script's comments, the original SLURM memory request of 8GB was omitted. This is a critical omission. Without a memory constraint, the job is at risk of being scheduled on a node with insufficient memory, leading to an out-of-memory failure.

The script is extremely non-portable. It uses a hardcoded, user-specific absolute path for the working directory (`/home/lynch/...`). It will fail for any other user or if the directory structure changes.

#!/bin/bash

# Copy/paste this job script into a text file and submit with the command:
#    sbatch thefilename
# job standard output will go to the file slurm-%j.out (where %j is the job ID)

#SBATCH --time=01:00:00   # walltime limit (HH:MM:SS)
#SBATCH --nodes=1   # number of nodes
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=18   # 36 processor core(s) per node 
#SBATCH --mem=8G   # maximum memory per node
#SBATCH --job-name="glap_bol_lin"
#SBATCH --output="laporta_grid_study_nvib_bolsig_linear.out"

module load matlab/R2022a
module load intel
export omp_num_threads=8
cd /home/lynch/boltzmann_solvers/mtmhbe_solver/performance/laporta/grid_study/nvib_sweep_data/
matlab -nodisplay -nosplash -nodesktop -r "laporta_bolsig_linear;exit;"
